knowledgeCards.title: Geyser
knowledgeCards.body: A geyser is a hot spring that erupts with steam and water. Pohutu, at Whakarewarewa in Rotorua, is one of the best known. This street is about 390 m long and meets Crummer Road and Rose Road.

knowledgeCards.title: Pavlova
knowledgeCards.body: Pavlova is a crisp meringue cake with a soft centre, usually topped with cream and fruit. It is a favourite on Christmas tables here. This street is about 1480 m long and meets Sussex Street and Scanlan Street.

knowledgeCards.title: Pikelet
knowledgeCards.body: A pikelet is a small, thick pancake. Here it is often served warm with butter, jam and cream. This street is about 680 m long and meets Rose Road.

knowledgeCards.title: Lollies
knowledgeCards.body: Lollies is the New Zealand word for sweets. A mixed bag from the dairy is a familiar treat. This street is about 730 m long and meets Richmond Road and Rose Road.

knowledgeCards.title: Sweet as
knowledgeCards.body: Sweet as is casual New Zealand slang for all good or great. This street is about 870 m long and meets Pollen Street, MacKelvie Street and Scanlan Street.

knowledgeCards.title: Ponsonby, Auckland
knowledgeCards.body: The fog has lifted on a real neighbourhood of wooden villas, cafés and a busy village street, just west of the city centre: Ponsonby, Auckland.
